4. PCS SIGNAL INTERFACE CONTROL DESCRIPTION The SCADA- PCS Misc. PLC system  consists of  hardware  and softwa re connections to other systems in 
the MCCPDC M3 Fill Line Facility.   This document describes hardware and software signals that are 
not part of other PCS sub- systems (i.e., EMS ) and what actions are taken by this system in response to 
those inputs.   
 Since an Administrator or Maintenance person may put any input point in SIMULATE and change its value, it is the responsibility of th is person to supervise and adjust the manually inserted value for any 
points placed in SIMULATE .  Failure to properly super vise and adjust manually inserted values may 
cause incorrect control functions and may lead to equipment damage.  
 Where vendor controller status information is required  for HMI display  and alarming , the FactoryTalk 
Linx communications driver will be utilized  and communication link status (active/ lost) will be read 
from the FactoryTalk Linx driver itself.   
 Where vendor information is required for control (Clean Steam Generator requesting Water For Injection delivery) , the connection is from the PCS -CP01 controller to vendor ’s controller and logic is 
implemented to know if the communication link is active or not.  Presently , this is only required on two 
vendor system, WFI and Parts Washer/Sterilizer.  The communication link status with logic is described in the MCCPDC WFI Control Block Narrative.docx document for those systems.  The PCS  Signals Interface  sub- system operates  in only one mode : Monitoring. 
 
4.1 Process Description and Strategy Design  
4.1.1 Weigh/Dispense System  
4.1.1.1 Common Trouble Signal  
The PCS system has a hardwired input signal from the Weigh/Dispense system which indicates the status of the Weigh/Dispense module.  The signal is named: 
“Weigh/Dispense Common Trouble Signal”  (XA -30001- 8).  When this signal is received, 
the PCS Light Tree Amber light shall be illuminated and an alarm banner shall be displayed on the PCS HMI screens.

4.1.2 Filler Signals  
4.1.2.1 Filler Run Status  
The PCS system has a software input signal from the Filler PLC which indicates the running status of the system.  The signal is named: “ Filler Run Status” 
(Filler_Stat_Running).  If the Filler Run Status  signal indicates the system is no longer  
running (1= Running, 0=Not running) the HMI indicator will change state to indicate no 
longer running.  
 4.1.2.2 Filler Common Trouble Alarm Signal  
The PCS system has a software input signal from  the Filler  PLC which indicates the 
trouble/alarm status of the system.  The signal is named: “ Filler Common Trouble 
Alarm” ( Filler _Sys_OK ).  If the Filler  Common Trouble alarm signal indicates trouble  
(1=System OK, 0=Trouble), the HMI Filler Common Trouble Alarm indicator will 
change state to indicate alarm and an alarm ba nner entry shall be displayed on the PCS 
HMI screens.  
 4.1.2.3 Filler Particulate Count High Alarm Signal  
The PCS system has a software input signal from the Filler PL C which indicates if the 
particulate count from the Filler particle counter instrument is indicating a high level of particulates.  
 4.1.2.4 Filler Vaporous Hydrogen Peroxide (VHP) Concentration  
The PCS system has a software input signal from the Filler PLC which indicates the concentration of the  Vaporous Hydrogen Peroxide (VHP) as detected by the Filler 
sensors.  (After change request processing this signal will be changing from a software signal to a hardware signal.)    Additional discussion regarding this signal can be found in 
the Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) Control Block Narrative.

4.1.9 Data Loggin g 
The PCS shall historically record quality data and system alarms.  All data shall be 
available to user via displays.  The logging of data points is not set in the PLC but rather in the FactoryTalk Historian Site Edition (SE) software product.  See MCCPDC PCS -
CP01 Alarms Hard Soft IO Listing.xlsx to determine which input, output, and internal points shall be configured to be logged in the Historian software product.   
4.2 Tasks/Routines/Functions  
The inputs will be assigned with MapIn and MapOut routines  as described according to the 
Controller Guidelines document.    For this work the following specific routines are expected:  
 R110_MapInLAD  
 R111_MapInFBD

Each of the input signals is displayed in engineering units on the HMI.  As mentioned 
previously, with the proper credentials, the input points can be simulated for calibration or other 
maintenance activities .   
4.4 Messages  and Alarming  
The messages and alarms have been combined into the overall PCS  system  document named 
MCCPDC PCS -CP01 A larm Listing  which provides among other details, the alarm text  and the 
input point tag identifier associated with the alarm.   Software alarms read from vendor systems 
are handled in the FactoryTalk Alarm and Events Server.  
 
4.5 Calculations  
There are no special calculations for this control strategy.   
 
4.6 Sequencers  
There are no sequencers for this control strategy.  
5. SOFTWARE PERMISSIVES  
The Signal Interface portion of the system does not have any software permissives. 
6. INTER -NETWORK RELATIONSHIPS  
The PCS -PLC receives signals from the vendor/OEM skid control systems within the facility via peer -
to-peer communication.  For each vendor skid the PCS  PLC is reading soft I/O values from, heartbeat -
type logic shall be implemented to ensure a n active connection exists and data values are live.  See the 
relevant section above for a particular machine’s signals.    
7. HARDWARE INTERLOCKS  
The Signal Interface portion of the system does not have any hardware interlocks.

methods

EMS  – Environmental Monitoring System

P&ID  - Piping and Instrumentation Diagram   
PAC  - Programmable Automation Controller  (used for higher -level , process -type control functionality 
compared to PLCs, approaching or equal to DCS functionality.  Sometimes the PAC and PLC 
terminology is used interchangeably.)

Control Panel 01)  
PLC - Programmable Logic Controller  (used for lower -level logic control ; sometimes the PAC and PLC 
terminology is used interchangeably.)  
Programming -  Developing software logic or source code  
SCADA – Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition  
VHP  – Vaporized  Hydrogen Peroxide

4.1.4 Vial Labeler Signals  
4.1.4.1 Vial Labeler Run Status  
Per reply to RFI -006, the PCS system shall read a software input signal from the Vial 
Labeler System which indicates the running status of the system.  The signal is named: 
“Vial Labeler Run Status” (Vial Label _Stat_Running).  If the Vial Labeler Run Status  
signal indicates the system is no longer  running (1=Running, 0=Not running) the HMI 
indicator will change state to indicate no longer running.  4.1.4.2 Vial / Syringe Labeler Common Trouble Alarm Signal  
Per reply to RFI -006, the PCS system shall read a software i nput signal from the Vial 
Labeler System  which indicates the trouble/alarm status of the system.  The signal is 
named: “Vial Common Trouble Alarm” ( VialLabel _Sys_OK ).  If the Vial  Common 
Trouble alarm signal indicates trouble  (1=System OK, 0=Trouble), the HMI Vial Labeler 
Common Trouble Alarm indicator will change state to indicate alarm and an alarm banner entry shall be displayed on the PCS HMI screens.

4.1.8 Cold Room Storage Signals  
4.1.8.1 Cold Room Storage Run Status  
The PCS system has a software input signal from the Cold Room Storage PLC which 
indicates the running status of the system.  The signal is named: “Cold Room Storage Run Status” (CRS_Stat _Running).  If the Cold R oom Storage Run Status  signal indicates 
the system is no longer  running (1=Running, 0=Not running) the HMI indicator will 
change state to indicate no longer running.  
 4.1.8.2 Cold Room Storage Common Trouble Alarm Signal  
The PCS system has a software input signal from  the Cold Room Storage PLC which 
indicates the trouble/alarm status of the system.  The signal is named: “Cold Room Storage Common Trouble Alarm” ( CRS_ Sys_OK ).  If the Cold Room Storage Common 
Trouble alarm signal indicates trouble  (1=System OK,  0=Trouble), the HMI Cold Room 
Storage Common Trouble Alarm indicator will change state to indicate alarm and an alarm ba nner entry shall be displayed on the PCS HMI screens.
